question: The chemical composition of the ruby gemstone is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aluminium oxide**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical composition of the **ruby gemstone** is **aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃)**.
 
• Rubies are a variety of the mineral corundum, which is primarily composed of aluminium oxide.
 
• The red color of rubies is due to the presence of trace amounts of **chromium** within the aluminium oxide structure.
 
• Rubies are one of the four precious gemstones, alongside sapphires, emeralds, and diamonds.
 
• They are highly valued for their color, hardness (second only to diamonds), and rarity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rubies** have been used in jewelry for centuries and are also used in various industrial applications due to their hardness.
 
• The most valuable rubies are those with a deep red color known as "pigeon's blood" red.
 
• Rubies are primarily mined in countries like Myanmar, Thailand, Sri Lanka, and Madagascar.
 
• In addition to their aesthetic value, rubies are also believed to have various metaphysical properties, including promoting energy, vitality, and courage.
 
• The largest known ruby is the "Liberty Bell Ruby," which weighs over 8,500 carats.
